audit.scope: modules/, pkgs/, helper/, .github/, test/ci, dev/, examples/, docs/

findings.title: lnd REST bound to 0.0.0.0 under wireguard preset; accept rule not interface-scoped
findings.detail: Enabling lndconnect with the wireguard preset sets restAddress=0.0.0.0 and tor.enforce=false, so the macaroon-admin REST API is protected only by the nixos-fw accept rule for the wg subnet, which matches source subnet without '-i wg-nb'. Spoofed-source packets on the external interface are kept out by rp_filter/routing, and TCP cannot complete a blind handshake, so practical impact is near nil. Deliberately deferred with a breakage checklist in docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md; the recommended shape (extra restlisten via extraConfig, keep restAddress local) is documented there.
findings.recommendation: Work the docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md checklist; scope the accept rule with -i wg-nb when touching it.

findings.title: test.yml lacks a top-level permissions block
findings.detail: The other two workflows set least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN permissions; test.yml relies on repo defaults. The job never uses the token and actions are SHA-pinned, so residual risk is small; fork PRs get a read-only token regardless.
findings.recommendation: Add 'permissions: { contents: read }' for consistency with the repo's own CI posture.

findings.title: Trim residue: dead code and stale references
findings.location: modules/netns-isolation.nix:98 (dead mkCliExec); examples/deploy-krops.sh, examples/deploy-container.sh (invoke removed lightning-cli); SECURITY.md (references deleted helper/push-release.sh)
findings.detail: No security impact, but the fork's security model is aggressive deletion; leftovers erode it and the demo scripts now print a failing command.
findings.recommendation: Delete mkCliExec, drop the lightning-cli demo lines, update SECURITY.md.

findings.title: Docs show rpc.address=0.0.0.0 / allowip 0.0.0.0/0 without scoping caveat
findings.detail: The example exposes bitcoind RPC at whatever scope the operator's firewall permits; the 'public' RPC user intentionally retains getpeerinfo/getnodeaddresses (lnd health checks), which leaks peer topology at that scope. Authentication is HMAC with ~119-bit passwords, so this is a documentation caveat, not a vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence noting the public whitelist's exposure scope follows the firewall rule.

findings.title: HEAD-adjacent security commits re-verified
findings.location: test/ci/cve-scan.sh, pkgs/btcpayserver/, pkgs/overrides.nix, pkgs/lndinit/, modules/onion-addresses.nix, modules/lnd.nix, pkgs/netns-exec/, modules/secrets/secrets.nix
findings.detail: cve-scan fail-open fixes correct (affected_by-only filter; rc/JSON fail-closed). btcpayserver 2.4.3 override correctly re-calls the package function and is version-guarded. Onion-hostname validation fails closed against multi-line config injection and closes the check-then-read TOCTOU. Macaroon staging uses root-only mktemp dir + atomic rename. netns-exec: exact whitelist, absolute-path exec, caps dropped. Secrets: no argv passwords, escaped interpolations, unknown files locked to root:0440. lnd custom-macaroon hex-decode pipeline confirmed exercised by the btcpayserver VM test.

summary.note: The only low (F1) is already documented and deliberately deferred with a correct analysis. The fork's audit-driven hygiene (version-guarded overrides, fail-closed CI scanning, per-CVE whitelist scoping) is in good shape at this commit; flake pins are ~7-10 days old, consistent with the stated weekly cadence.
